Key Research Thinking Patterns: Combinatorial Positivity Proofs: Establishing the positivity of cluster variables and Laurent polynomials by constructing explicit combinatorial bases, such as using snake graphs and hypergraph generalizations to enumerate admissible matchings and verify positivity conjectures in Graph LP algebras.

Geometric-Combinatorial Bijection Construction: Mapping complex algebraic structures to discrete combinatorial objects to solve enumeration problems, exemplified by constructing bijections between Deodhar components of braid varieties and vertex-labeled trees to derive classical identities like Cayley’s formula.

Poset-Theoretic Basis Unification: Unifying geometric arc resolutions with order ideal enumeration by employing fence posets and distributive lattices to derive explicit skein relations and basis constructions (bangles/bracelets) for cluster algebras on punctured surfaces.

Scattering Diagram and Broken Line Methodology: Extending the Gross-Hacking-Keel-Kontsevich (GHKK) framework to reciprocal generalized cluster algebras by utilizing cluster scattering diagrams and broken lines to construct theta function bases and prove mutation invariance.
Summary Description: Elizabeth Kelley specializes in pure mathematics, bridging combinatorics, algebraic geometry, and representation theory. Her work extends the GHKK framework to reciprocal generalized cluster algebras, utilizing scattering diagrams and broken lines to establish positivity. She employs snake graphs and hypergraph generalizations for combinatorial positivity proofs in Graph LP algebras. Recently, she expanded into affine Kac-Moody groups, constructing bijections between Deodhar components of braid varieties and vertex-labeled trees. By applying Opdam’s trace formula and Haglund’s identity, she provides elaborate new proofs for classical combinatorial identities like Cayley’s formula. Additionally, she addresses positivity in Laurent phenomenon (LP) algebras by defining rooted clusters for tree-encoded graphs. In her latest work, she pioneers the use of fence posets and distributive lattices to derive explicit skein relations and basis constructions (bangles/bracelets) for cluster algebras on punctured surfaces, unifying geometric arc resolutions with poset-theoretic expansions.
